title: Approval grant ledger (RoE §2 human-in-the-loop record)
description: The AUDIT record of operator approvals for gated (exploitation / post-exploitation / prod-touch / destructive) actions, written to <engagement>/runtime/approvals.json BEFORE the first gated action (see roe-gate.md §2). This is the human grant trail the reviewers read — distinct from the launcher's autonomous-deferral store (approvals.py's {approved, resume_queue} fingerprint list), which may share the same file; the root is left open so both can coexist. Each grant carries the reversibility contract: a write-to-prove is only approvable as a reversible-self-write WITH a recorded delete_path (see write-vs-probe.md).

phase.description: The gated phase this grant authorizes, e.g. exploitation / post-exploitation.

scope_granted.description: Exactly what was authorized (target + action), in the operator's words.

method.description: How the grant was obtained (chat / email / ticket / signed-RoE ref).

granted_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp — MUST pre-date the first gated action.

intent.description: probe = cannot persist state (see write-vs-probe.md); write = a real production write.

write_class.description: The persistence class of the approved action. 'reversible-self-write' is INVALID without a recorded delete_path.

reversible.description: Whether the approved action's state change is reversible. If true, a delete_path OR cleanup_method MUST be recorded.

delete_path.description: The EXACT route/command/id that reverses the write (probed + recorded BEFORE the write, executed right after). Required for a reversible-self-write.

cleanup_method.description: A human-readable cleanup route when delete_path is not a single call (e.g. 'operator deletes the test record via the admin UI').

justification.description: Why this action is needed and why a lower-persistence probe (readback / validation-failing body) does NOT already suffice.
